title: What Is the Salary Seek? Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay in Australia

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your salary. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, above which no extra super is required.

bodyMarkdown:
## What Is the Salary Seek? Understanding Your Pay Conversion

When you’re offered an hourly rate or a salary, the question “what is the salary seek” often comes down to understanding how those numbers translate into annual, fortnightly, and take-home amounts. In Australia, the standard approach for full-time work is a 38-hour week, and the Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. This article explains the conversion formula, the difference between minimum and award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax – so you can compare offers with confidence.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use this simple calculation:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. This matches the weekly rate of $1004.90 multiplied by 52. 

If you work part-time or casual, adjust the hours per week to your actual average. The same formula applies – just use your regular weekly hours.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Check

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Using the minimum wage example: $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers quoted per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services (SCHADS) Award have their own classification rates that may exceed the national minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

Always check which award applies to your job. Your employer must pay at least the award rate for your classification. The National Minimum Wage only applies if no award or registered agreement covers you.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. This loading is added to the base rate, not the other way around. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the “casual loading” box to automatically add 25% to the hourly rate you enter – do not type a rate that already includes loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For the 2026–27 financial year, the maximum contribution base is $270,830 – earnings above that do not attract compulsory super. So if your annual gross is $52,245, your employer must contribute an extra $6,269.40 (12%) into your super fund. This is separate from your take-home pay.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your gross annual salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The tax-free threshold of $18,200 means you pay no tax on that portion. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net income after tax and Medicare.

### Putting It All Together: An Example

Let’s say you are a full-time employee earning $30 per hour, working 38 hours per week, with casual loading (if applicable).

- **Annual gross**: $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280
- **Fortnightly gross**: ($30 × 38) × 2 = $2,280
- **Super (12%)**: $59,280 × 0.12 = $7,113.60 (paid on top)
- **Estimated tax (2026–27)**: On $59,280, tax is approximately $7,717 (using the scale: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, then 30% on $14,280 = $4,284, total $8,304 less low-income offset? We won't calculate precisely here – use the ATO calculator.)
- **Medicare levy (2%)**: $1,185.60
- **Estimated take-home**: $59,280 – $8,304 – $1,185.60 = $49,790.40 per year, or about $957.50 per week.

### Important Notes

This conversion assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It also uses the standard 38-hour week. If your hours vary, use your average weekly hours. For award-covered employees, check your specific award for penalty rates and allowances that may increase your pay.

For more details on minimum wages and award classifications, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. To explore how super and salary packaging affect your total compensation, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Final Thoughts

Understanding “what is the salary seek” means knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and take-home figures. By using the formula hourly × hours per week × 52, and factoring in casual loading, super, and tax, you can make informed decisions about job offers and negotiate with confidence. Always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission for the most accurate and up-to-date rates.
